newsitem.title: UK: Gold up slightly at fix, follows platinum metals.
newsitem.headline: Gold up slightly at fix, follows platinum metals.

text.p: Gold edged higher on Wednesday as platinum and palladium took the leading role in precious metals markets, traders said.
Gold fixed a touch higher at $349.00 an ounce from $348.90 Wednesday afternoon. The rally that started on Friday sent bullion to a high of $350.90, where it met tough resistance.
Platinum group metals continued to strengthen despite an expected resumption in the delayed Russian exports by mid-June.
Dealers were nervous about any price gyrations engineered by speculative funds said to hold the upper hand in palladium.
"It's a very risky business at the moment," said a European trader. "You don't know what these speculators are going to do."
Platinum was $4.50 up in the morning at $393.50/$394.50, while palladium gained $4.00 to $174.00/$175.00.
The market largely shrugged off news on Tuesday that the Russian platinum metals export agency Almaz had started talks with key buyer Japan on 1997 sale contracts.
Russian exports have been delayed since December due to bureaucratic and political problems, prompting a tightening in short term lending rates for both platinum and palladium.
Although the news signalled lower prices, dealers said moves by the funds could move the market higher in the near term.
"We have very tight supplies. People want to borrow the metal and they can't wait until June," said the dealer.
But industry would shun palladium at prices above $180.
The funds could look into liquidating their long positions if they were convinced that the Japanese could build enough stocks after Russian deliveries start to satisfy domestic demand.
One-month palladium lease rates were quoted as high as 22-24 percent while platinum was at 12-13 percent.
Gold was shy of re-challenging stiff resistance above $350.00.
Renewed talk about a U.S. rate rise this month is likely to keep gold capped, with producer selling expected above $350.
Support from the weak dollar was also on the wane.
"There is a very strong resistance at $350.50," said one analyst, pointing to a six-month downtrend line at that level.
"But if we penetrate this level there is room to $354."
Dealers said gold was to a large extent likely to follow moves in platinum and palladium in the absence of other fundamentals, with support now safely established around $346.
Silver stood a touch higher at $4.86/$4.88. Dealers expected a positive report by Gold Fields Mineral Services due later on Wednesday.
"I'm expecting the gold/silver ratio to move in favour of silver," said the European dealer.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
